messages:
sam: Heads up — CS flagged a customer hitting 503s from the hosted inference API, multiple regions. They say it started ~10:02 UTC and is affecting live traffic :exclamation:

emma: Thanks Sam. Do we have the request IDs or any gateway logs?

sam: Pasting a sample curl response from the tenant's run:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 10:05:12 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "control_plane_dependency_error",
  "details": "auth-session-timeout -> routing-policy-503 -> configdb read timeout"
}
```
Request-id: r-4f7c2a9e (they've sent 20+ from different users)

maria: Noted. We're also seeing routing-policy service returning 500/503s on the dashboard around the same window. Likely cascade from config DB.

incident-bot: ALERT: control-plane.routing-policy high error rate (503) in us-west-2 — 10:02:40 to 10:08:30 — 82 errors/min — linked to config-db read latency spike

kai: Quick triage notes:
- configdb read latency jumped to 5s on several primary shards.
- auth-session handshake timeouts spiked concurrently, which makes the gateway fallback attempt to call routing-policy more often.
- routing-policy doesn't have a healthy fallback configured for these session errors so it surfaces 503 back to the gateway.

emma: Can you paste the relevant service logs for auth-session and routing-policy? Even a short snippet with timestamps helps. Also which pool of nodes for configdb was hot?

maria: Snippet from routing-policy logs:
```
2026-03-17T10:03:12Z ERROR routing-policy.handler: failed to evaluate route: configdb: read timeout (shard-3)
2026-03-17T10:03:13Z WARN  routing-policy.fallback: no fallback route configured for tenant 5421
2026-03-17T10:03:14Z ERROR routing-policy.http: responding 503 to gateway for request x-req-5421
```

sam: Customer impact: some inference calls retried by client, others saw immediate 503. They've paused production traffic. They asked for ETA and whether this is a billing/credits issue.

emma: Short-term mitigation options:
1) Enable token-cache local fallback in gateway (reduces auth-session calls) — low risk, config change.
2) Route traffic away from affected routing-policy nodes (scale down shards or throttle new reads).
3) Increase configdb read timeout as a stopgap (risky).

kai: I can flip (1) for the hosted gateway for that tenant and enable a lightweight fallback policy. Will monitor error rate.

maria: For longer-term, we need:
- routing-policy: implement cached route fallback for session-auth failures (A/B rollout).
- configdb: investigate shard hotness and read QPS, likely a bad query pattern from some tenants.

sam: Repro steps provided by CS (from customer):
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{...}' -v
2) observe 503 with control_plane_dependency_error 30-40% of attempts during spike
(They also sent heap and cpu graphs for nodes, attaching in ticket)

emma: Action items:
- kai: enable token-cache fallback for tenant 5421 and monitor (ETA 15m).
- maria: collect routing-policy logs + configdb slow query list + shard metrics, start postmortem (ETA 30m).
- sam: keep customer updated and request request-ids for failed calls so we can cross-reference (assign to CS).

kai: Done — enabled token-cache fallback for that tenant and temporarily bumped routing-policy replica read window. Early signal: error rate halved in us-west-2. Monitoring continues. :thumbsup:

maria: Collected slow query trace: a scan from an internal analytics job hit shard-3 causing read latencies. We've flagged the job and asked infra to throttle.

emma: Great. We'll keep this thread for final summary. If routing-policy errors drop to baseline and configdb latencies normalize, we'll notify CS and close.

sam: Customer updated — they confirmed traffic recovery and will re-run verification next hour. Thanks team.

maria: Postmortem outline: root cause = analytics scan causing configDB shard hotness -> auth-session timeouts -> routing-policy cascade -> gateway 503s. Remediation: throttle analytics, implement routing-policy cached fallback, and add circuit-breaker between auth-session and routing-policy.

sam: Adding final note: CS asked for a short incident email for customer and billing reassurance that no credits will be auto-applied; will draft and share.
